newsitem.title: CHINA: China paper sees new high on Hong Kong stock index.
newsitem.headline: China paper sees new high on Hong Kong stock index.

text.p: An official Chinese newspaper predicted on Monday that Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index would move between 13,000 and 16,500 points in the second half of 1997.

The Hong Kong stock index, buoyed by an influx of capital and the return of the former British colony to Chinese rule on July 1, would hit new highs before the end of the year, the Financial News said.
The Hang Seng index closed at a record finish of 15,370.94 on Monday, up 145.65 points.

The newspaper, published by the central bank, said in a signed commentary that the real estate market could hit stock prices though a possible consolidation would benefit the stable development of the share market.
But it said earnings of listed companies could eventually benefit from China's rapid economic growth as the two economies became even more closely entwined.
It also warned, however, that a short-term rise based solely on the psychological effects of the return of Hong Kong, could easily encourage an unsustainable bubble market.
